svg.title: Protein destinations and modification compartments
svg.desc: The conventional secretory route passes through ER and Golgi. N glycosylation begins in ER, mucin O glycosylation usually in Golgi, collagen hydroxylysine glycosylation in ER, and O GlcNAc on nuclear and cytosolic proteins in those compartments. Other routes include mitochondrial presequences through TOM and TIM23, classical nuclear localization signals through import receptors, and peroxisomal PTS1 and PTS2 signals.
svg.text: Protein targeting: location changes the mechanism
Cytosolic ribosome → ER entry → Golgi → destination
ER: N-linked glycan transfer; folding and quality control
Golgi: glycan processing, mucin-type O-glycans and sorting
ER entry may use a cleaved signal peptide or a retained signal-anchor.
Collagen: hydroxylysine O-glycans begin in ER.
Nuclear/cytosolic O-GlcNAc: added in those compartments.
The linkage class alone does not identify the cellular pathway.
PTS1 → PEX5; PTS2 → PEX7 pathway → peroxisome
These routes do not require passage through the Golgi.
Representative routes: each compartment also has important exceptions.
